newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Birch defends NZ's prospect of triple A rating.
newsitem.headline: Birch defends NZ's prospect of triple A rating.

text.p: Finance Minister Bill Birch on Friday rejected claims that New Zealand's chances of achieving a triple A credit rating were receding.
"New Zealand's chances of achieving a return to a Triple A credit raing are higher than ever," he said in a statement.
Birch was responding to comments made by Bob Mattew, the vice-chairman of the right-wing think tank, the Business Roundtable.
Birch repeated that four weeks ago rating agency Standard & Poor's told him that continuation of current policies of budget surpluses and reducing debt could lead to an improved rating.
"In the face of these assurances, it is plainly nonsense for Bob Matthew to claim that our chances of regaining a triple A credit rating are receding," Birch said.
"Standard & Poor's view is in direct contradiction to Mr Matthew's remarks."
Matthew seemed to be needlessly and irresponsibly fuelling overseas concern, he added.
On Thursday, S&P said New Zealand's long-term foreign currency debt rating of AA+ was not expected to change over the next three years.
S&P said in a report on New Zealand that the rating outlook was stable and the country had made impressive progress.
Matthew said in a speech in Sydney on Wednesday that New Zealand was showing signs of "losing the plot".

Matthew, who is also chairman of Brierley Investments and Air NZ, said that economic and social reform in both New Zealand and Australia was lagging behind more dynamic countries in Asia and elsewhere.
